blocks.text: Pitt Meadows condos and townhomes by price band, September 2026

14 condos and townhomes sold in September against 66 listed. The price band with the most sales was $600,001 to $700,000, with 4 sold (29% of the month). Among bands with at least ten homes listed, the highest sales ratio was $700,001 to $800,000 at 36%.

Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Pitt Meadows?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 66 condos and townhomes listed in Pitt Meadows and 14 sold in the month, a sales ratio of 21%. Month-end counts move daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: What is the reported sale price for condos and townhomes in Pitt Meadows?
faq.a: The September report gave $662,500 for condos and townhomes in Pitt Meadows, against $572,500 the month before. The reports give one sale-price figure and do not say whether it is an average or a median, so use it for direction, not as a valuation of your own home.

faq.q: How long do condos and townhomes take to sell in Pitt Meadows?
faq.a: The September report showed 40 days on market for condos and townhomes in Pitt Meadows and a sale-to-list price ratio of 97%, against 28 days the month before.

faq.q: What should I read before buying a condo in Pitt Meadows?
faq.a: The Form B, the bylaws, the last two years of strata minutes, the depreciation report and the contingency reserve fund balance. They show planned repairs, special levies and rules on pets and rentals.

faq.q: What do strata fees cover on a condo in Pitt Meadows?
faq.a: Strata fees pay for upkeep and insurance of the common property and the contingency reserve fund, and in some buildings heat, hot water or other services. The Form B Information Certificate lists exactly what a unit's fee covers.
